title: 5 Best Small Business Marketing Apps | McQuillen Creative

facts.fact: MailChimp offers a free plan for small business owners with 2,000 contacts or less, according to the author.
facts.quote: If you’re a small business owner with a collection of 2,000 contacts or less, you can take advantage of a free plan

facts.fact: The author states that Hootsuite's social media power does not come free of charge.
facts.quote: none of that power comes to you for free.

facts.fact: The author states that Buffer has a free plan, but its features are somewhat limited on that plan.
facts.quote: Buffer’s features are a bit limited with their free plan.

facts.fact: The author says Adobe Spark plans start free, with more features available on paid plans.
facts.quote: Plans start free, but you can get more features with paid plans.

facts.fact: The author says the Microsoft Office mobile app's cloud storage integrations (such as Dropbox and OneDrive) require a Microsoft 365 subscription.
facts.quote: those cloud storage integrations come at a cost of a Microsoft 365 subscription.

facts.fact: The author states that Microsoft OneNote can be used completely free, with a Microsoft account adding functionality.
facts.quote: you can use this powerful app completely free.

facts.fact: The author states that Adobe Spark is included in Adobe Creative Cloud subscriptions.
facts.quote: Adobe Spark is rolled into the Adobe Creative Cloud subscriptions.

facts.fact: The author's hypothetical desert-island list contains five apps for small business marketing.
facts.quote: these are the five apps I would download to start.
